$comment: The Blueprint page's 16 sections, in the order they appear in the source PDF.
This file is the spine: the page renders from it and every assertion reads it, so
'the page has 16 sections in PDF order' cannot drift from what is checked.
TIERS ARE PRESENTATION, NEVER PRESENCE. All 16 render into the DOM in this order,
always. The tier decides prominence only:
1 = always visible. The linear path to a booking; a complete sales page on its own.
2 = native <details>, default-collapsed. In the DOM, openable with JavaScript off.
3 = compressed to summary cards whose depth lives on its own route.
This exists because two requirements pull against each other: every section must be
present, and they must not all shout at once. Those are only compatible if presence
and prominence are different things. The failure this guards against is buying
digestibility with scissors — so a test asserts the ordered id array, which goes red
if a section is deleted to make the page feel shorter.
